 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Throughout his media career, Gilbert Arenas has made many controversial takes that have gotten him in hot water. He once said the NBA needs to get rid of European players to solve its defensive problems. He also questioned Rudy Gobert missing a game to visit his newborn child and said Karl-Anthony Towns is built like a woman.​
 However, the take that drew Arenas the most flak was saying Michael Jordan is the second-greatest player of all time. Although he admitted to shifting his GOAT stance to play to the audience, he stood by his belief that LeBron James deserves the No. 1 spot in basketball history
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "I'm one of the audiences who grew up; you told us Michael Jordan was the greatest, and this is how you told us he was the greatest. Okay, I got that information," Arenas said on the "Get To The Point" podcast.
 Jordan was declared GOAT in 1988
 Arenas was only two years old when Jordan was drafted into the NBA, and only six when Jordan had his best individual regular-season ever in 1988.
 Arenas has previously argued that Jordan was crowned the GOAT after that historic season, years before winning his first championship. However, the conversation changed as new generations of stars emerged, with Kobe Bryant arriving in 1996 and LeBron James in 2003.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "My favorite player went from Penny Hardaway to Kobe Bryant," he added. "I know they don't have the same body type, so this is a different engine. Now this engine is not like this, but it has to work so much more to even get in this zone. So the fact that he even got in the GOAT conversation, that's GOAT s — t. Then a LeBron James comes." 
 "You said he is Magic Johnson with Michael Jordan's ability. What I watched was Magic Johnson with Michael Jordan's ability. He did not disappoint, whatsoever. There's nobody who can say in the 24 years that they went into the season and failed expectations that season. If you want to try to say that championships is what failed, the 82 games plus doing what he did, that man never failed. Not one time, not one season you can say was bad. That's GOAT s — t." 
 Related: "MFers should stand still" – Jason Williams thinks NBA fined LeBron James for disrespecting national anthem 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement LeBron's consistency
 Although his critics always point to his 4-6 record in the NBA Finals as the reason he can't be the GOAT, James has led his teams to tremendous success in the regular season.
 After his rookie year, every team James played for from 2004-05 through 2017-18 finished with a winning record and reached the playoffs. He also finished at least in the Top 6 in MVP voting in each of those 13 years and received at least one MVP vote every season from age 18 to 37 while several all-time greats were still in their primes​.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "Think about who's in the NBA. When we talk about top fives of anything, Kobe Bryant's there. Tim Duncan, Shaquille O'Neal, Allen Iverson, Dirk, KG. You know he won MVPs while they were in their prime, being dominant champions. While they was fighting for who's going to be the king on top, nobody realized the young bull is winning the most valuable player," Arenas continued.
 So who is Arenas' GOAT?
 Arenas then concluded his GOAT discussion with an intriguing closing argument.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "So when you talk about our great players, we defend the one we love and target the one we don't like. But when we listen to how we sound, we are forgetting that the n—a is No.2," he concluded.
 People disagree with who the greatest of all time is. But everybody is entitled to their opinion, including Arenas.
